headline: On November 17, 1989: Student protest in Prague sparks Velvet Revolution
captionCards: 41 years of one-party rule ended peacefully
Non-violent transition inspired democratic movements worldwide
instagramCaption:
Students in Prague defy communist rule.

A demonstration by students in Prague on November 17, 1989, was met with violent crackdowns by riot police. This moment ignited widespread public protests across Czechoslovakia, involving both youth and older dissidents. The uprising lasted until November 28, leading to the end of 41 years of one-party communist rule. Remarkably, the transition was non-violent, culminating in a peaceful handover of power on December 29.

It reshaped Central Europe’s political landscape, paving the way for democracy and market reforms.
